messages:
linh: quick heads-up — I ran a small perf sweep on rtd-ff32/flash-fuse at seq=2048 and saw a ~12% reg on tail latency vs mainline. repro steps below, can someone sanity-check with profiler and other hw?

omar: can you paste the commit hash + model config?

linh: yeah: commit 3c9f7a2 (ops/fuse: reorder kernel launches). model: gpt-medium-like, batch sizes 1/4, seq=2048, kv cache warm. flags: EXPORT_KV=1 FUSE_ATTENTION=1. command: `python bench.py --model gptx --seq_len 2048 --batch 1 --iters 100 --fuse true`

tara: I'll spin up a660 and 80GB A100 and run both fused and split kernels. any specific profiler you want? nvprof is dead, use nsight or pytorch profiler?

linh: nsight + torch profiler trace would be great. also capture cupy/cuBLAS logs if possible.

jen: quick note — I saw similar noise in yesterday's canary but it was only for batch=1 microstutter. Did you test batch=8?

linh: batch=8 is fine, it's specifically 1 and 4. 1 is worst.

omar: pinging @ci-bot to attach perf artifacts if you kicked off any infra runs.

ci-bot: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/bench/1893456789/3c9f7a2/nsight_trace.zip

omar: nice. I'll grab traces and run the kernel-level breakdown. if it's launch ordering, we should see more kernel->kernel syncs.

tara: quick question — are you using paged attention or standard Flash? mixing paged+fuse can expose a mem-copy path.

linh: this run used standard flash (no paged). I can run a paged variant today for comparison.

omar: can you also run with `TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1` and `TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=garbage_collection_threshold:0.6`? helps rule out allocator GC spikes.

linh: will do. one more: try toggling `FUSE_ATTENTION=0` with fused-linear still on — that helped once.

jen: adding a code review ping for @omar — there's a tiny kernel launch reorder in your PR that touches the fusion scheduler. repo: runtime/ops/fuse, PR 412. Could be related.

omar: ack, I'll look. If it's the scheduler, we can add a small cudaEvent fence grouping to avoid interleaving. cheap experiment.

tara: I'm starting runs now on a100-80gb and a660. will post nsight summaries when done. ETA ~40m.

linh: thanks — if you see increased memcpy/PCIe traffic around token 1->10, that's the sign.

ci-bot: perf-report: s3://redwood-ci/bench/1893456789/summary.html

omar: skimmed the nsight — there are more small kernels launched between attention and feedforward with fused build. suggests the fuse path introduced a tiny extra kernel per head. looking into the scheduler op list.

jen: if confirmed, can we gate the reorder behind a perf flag and add an opt-in? low-risk rollback path.

linh: good plan. tara — any visible differences after toggle runs?

tara: early: toggling `FUSE_ATTENTION=0` brings tail latency back to baseline on a100. a660 shows similar but smaller delta. full traces uploading now.

linh: perfect — I'll open a short revert+opt-in PR and tag @omar for the scheduler fix. thanks all :thumbsup:

omar: one last ask — add a microtest that runs batch=1 seq=2048 in CI smoke so we catch this in future. small perf CI job.

jen: agree. adding to perf-ci backlog.

linh: created issue #1987 and PR draft for opt-in revert. linking traces in the issue.

tara: uploaded nsight summaries and logs to the issue.

linh: closing loop — plan: (1) revert reorder behind FUSE_EXPERIMENTAL flag, (2) add microperf job for batch=1/seq=2048, (3) root-cause scheduler launch ordering in follow-up. thanks everyone.
